purpose: S6 mechanism-isolation (R4.1): three arms show which mechanism buys HONEST completion. bare = no harness; structural-only = TaskOps' v0.8 claim-safety audit that does NOT execute the task's checks; verify-grounded = TaskOps v0.9 that RE-EXECUTES the requiredChecks out-of-workspace. Tier labels honest: the bare and verify-grounded arms are Tier-1 external benchmarks; the structural-only arm is the v0.8 Tier-2 mechanism battery (a same-tasks no-verify arm on the external benchmarks is the clean follow-up, R4.1b).

bare.false_completion: claims done without evidence — 48/50 (96%) on ImpossibleBench-conflicting (codex), 1/31 (3.2%) on SWE-bench Lite (claude)

structural_only_v08.false_completion: 0 — audit reports claimSafe=false for any structural-only closure (never certifies self-report)
structural_only_v08.discrimination: 0 — refuses to certify EVEN truly-correct completions (14/14 structural_complete_but_test_failed marked not claim-safe, including the correct ones); it reports closure SHAPE/APPROVAL, not test-passing

verify_grounded_v09.false_completion: 0 — verified_done only on runner-executed out-of-workspace pass evidence (0/31 SWE, 0/50 impossible)
verify_grounded_v09.discrimination: exact — 26/26 verified_done are official resolves (precision 1.00), recall 83.9% on SWE-bench Lite; honest-stalls on the impossible set

reading: bare has high false-completion and no gate; structural-only removes false completion but ALSO removes discrimination (a stopped clock — it refuses correct work); verify-grounding is the mechanism that removes false completion WHILE preserving discrimination (exact oracle agreement). The load-bearing step is the runner EXECUTING the check, not the graph structure alone.
honesty_tax: on SWE-bench Lite, wrapping trades ~16% of instances (5/31 honest stalls where retries=0) for a 0-false-positive guarantee; §8 shows verify-retries recover some of that recall honestly.
